# ForzaPort 0.10.16.5 experimental RC

The normal conversion and incremental installer retain the instrument, wheel, materials, UV, driver-consistency and Undo-history work from 0.10.15. Conversion, structural validation and gameplay acceptance remain distinct.

## Optional suspension experiment

Settings exposes Experimental suspension / steering, off by default. Prepare / update runtime explicitly offers a ForzaPort steering overlay built against pinned current Extra Options 0.2.98 source. The official standard runtime remains available. Known host/proxy signatures, backups and rollback guards remain enforced; vendor Azimuth files and saves are not replaced.

The converter detects Drift by the source steering profile's semantic name, creates a missing drift choice using the native Race menu presentation and translates compatible physics through the regular upgrade adapter. Its source angle limits are stored per suspension, including normal-limit restoration. Native response rates and animation travel remain approximations. Missing or ambiguous native templates are reported/refused, not guessed.

Steering maps are validated, sealed and rebased during recipient Add Car. The runtime reads narrowly scoped car-owned .fpsteering sidecars. Loose car geometry folders remain staging-only. Undo removes only receipt-owned files/rows. Returning to the standard runtime is refused while active experimental imports depend on it.

## Four-wheel steering boundary

Source stock and optional suspension rear-steering profiles are preserved in reports. Physical rear steering and rear-wheel steering animation are NOT implemented: their native force/orientation integration points are unverified. No front-angle approximation is called four-wheel steering.

## Acceptance

Test using original source archives through the GUI. Compare stock, experimental additional Race suspension, then stock again; check turning circle, steering movement, both camera views and retention after returning to the garage. Rear steering is not expected to appear. Analogue/digital displays, AO, dirt/vinyl and arbitrary-car compatibility still need gameplay acceptance.

All supplied dependency credits/notices and runtime corresponding source are retained. The EXE is unsigned. The maintainer confirms dependency licences/permissions; each tester supplies their own source game resources. Agent checks use synthetic targets; no real conversion, game launch or installed-car modification is part of this checkpoint.

## 0.10.16.5 corrections

Supported source class badges now retain their semantic identity and relative raw-band position. Preserving absolute source display scores previously demoted source S1 to native A because the games use different display ceilings. Source-only classes retain an explicitly reported numeric fallback; runtime physics PI remains unmeasured.

Supported aero choices select complete source geometry, including shared stock models and removal-only/empty selections. Stock render-model multiplicity and bindings must remain unchanged after migration and serialization. Category-owned database evidence may remove inactive shared selectors; reachable geometry is unchanged and live database choices missing scene branches still fail. A matching helper capability is required.

The user confirmed the earlier Lamborghini output operates in game; AO remains unconfirmed. These new corrections have offline regression coverage, not gameplay acceptance. Reconvert the original source in the GUI; old exported ZIPs retain their previous conversion.

## 0.10.16.5 naming

Source localization now supplies the model-only label. Exact source manufacturer/year prefixes are separated using database metadata because FH2 displays these separately. Internal model words/numbers and explicit custom labels are preserved. Original localized label and identity metadata remain in the conversion report. Existing ZIPs retain their previous labels; reconvert the original archive in the GUI. This release does not upgrade offline validation to gameplay verification; AO and experimental features retain their stated test limits.

## Visual serialization guard correction

The full-selection validator compared an unused legacy AOSwatchPath empty string against null after parsing version 15 models, although that field is not serialized for version 9 onward. The comparison now follows the format version and includes the actual AOMapInfos list. Synthetic regressions compare full stock and optional render bindings through serialization. No geometry checks are removed. Reconvert using the GUI; runtime acceptance remains separate.

## 0.10.16.5 compatibility checkpoint

Donor engine placement and driven axles are semantic requirements, not soft score penalties. Incompatible foundations are refused; some archives previously accepted may now lack a supported donor. Native menu fallback stays in the same visual category, reports its native level/manufacturer presentation and preserves source geometry/common aero. Single-wheel-axle widths above 0.05 m pass the shared finite/unit guard; zero/invalid dimensions still fail.

A new normal-pipeline lamp pass adapts previously supported simple source emitter roles to available selected-donor bulb materials and draw buckets, preserving geometry and reporting unknown/masked channels. Native textures/colours and beam rig are approximations; gameplay response is unverified. Retro Rally maps explicitly to native 90s Rally/Iconic Rally as an approximation, rather than retaining Group B. Steering output paths follow source wheel paths; this does not establish rotational fidelity or driver hand alignment.

Recipient allocation reserves historical receipt-owned IDs, including removed imports, because Undo does not remove owned cars from saves. This prevents future stale-ID reuse but does not repair existing garage entries or prove the cause of observed catalogue/garage PI differences. Catalogue/owned PI reconciliation remains unresolved; no runtime PI calculation or save patch is claimed. Fresh stock purchase under a newly reserved ID is the next diagnostic, performed by the user. These limits remain release/testing caveats.
